translations.answer: Do not directly call the API with a full-zero tensor and a single env_ids, as the global has_external_wrench may be disabled. A workaround has been tested and verified: maintain a full shape=(num_envs, ...) force/torque buffer, set the target environment row to zero, and call without env_ids. The code modification is proposed to use the updated internal buffer, but it is uncertain in terms of compatibility and not verified by maintainers, so it is only noted as a candidate fix.
translations.applicability: Corresponds to Isaac Lab commit a466d4e / Isaac Sim 5.0. New versions require checking function semantics and minimal reproduction.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent reproduction is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: Participants suggest constructing a full num_envs tensor; the author notes that passing a full tensor with a single env_ids leads to shape mismatch and modifies to call without env_ids.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author proposes modifying the internal buffer to check _external_force_b/_external_torque_b, but this is not verified for compatibility.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between internal force/torque buffer per environment and the global has_external_wrench switch; check if the second call input is all-zero and if the first dimension of the tensor matches the env_ids.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The author explicitly tests and verifies a workaround: retain the full num_envs force/torque buffer, set the target environment row to zero, and call without env_ids.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab main commit a466d4e; Isaac Sim 5.0; and RigidObject in parallel environments.
translations.details.limits.0: Writing back the full buffer increases data management cost; the source code modification is only a possible fix and not a merged solution.
translations.details.limits.1: The InteractiveScene.reset already resets the buffer, so no additional call is needed.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author confirms that calling with the full buffer and without env_ids works; the local env_ids API semantics are not yet verified for the fix.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does setting zero external force/torque for only resetting env_ids clear external wrenches for all other environments? What is the actual workaround?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Record actual wrenches for each environment during disturbance or safety recovery testing; do not infer external forces from call parameters alone.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The current implementation sets the global has_external_wrench based on the current input forces.any()/torques.any(), rather than the updated full internal buffer.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Calling with zero force/torque for env 0 and env_ids results in all non-reset environments having zero external wrench.
translations.source.locator: Issue #4392, full buffer workaround and issuecomment-3757880219
